newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK NAFTA PLAN FAILS TO CALM ANALYSTS.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK NAFTA PLAN FAILS TO CALM ANALYSTS.

text.p: Slovak oil and gas storage firm Nafta a.s. announced an ambitious eight-year investment plan to shareholders on Wednesday, but analysts said the move did little to shore up the firm's sagging image.

Nafta has been surrounded by controversy since the government sold its 45.9 percent stake to the private and little known company Druha Obchodna for 500 million crowns, far below its market value of about 3.2 billion crowns.
Analysts had seen Wednesday's extraordinary shareholders' meeting as a chance to show its vision of the firm's future, but came away less than impressed.

They said that despite unveiling a one billion crown investment programme over the next eight years, the company's owners failed to show stronger commitment to the development of the company, nor did it reveal specifics on the plan.

"They had a chance to clear up the uncertainty surrounding them, they could have shown the market their real committment to the development of the company," one international broker who attended the meeting told Reuters.
"But it seems that they have failed in this task."
The state privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF), raised eyebrows in August when it sold its entire holdings in Nafta, to Druha Obchodna.
The sell-off implied an average price of about 400 crowns a share, while at the time of the sale, Nafta shares stood at around 2,000 crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE).
Dusan Sykora, a broker at ING Barings, said that owners of Nafta did not just fail to dispell negative rumours about them, but that their presentation may have even further damage Nafta's image.
"We can expect that investors will sell their holdings in Nafta, as nothing is much clearer, if not even worse," he said.
Over the last four months since Nafta's privatisation, the new owners have made very little clear what is their long-term strategy with the firm analysts said.

In turn, they said, investor interest in Nafta shares has waned, resulting in a sharp fall in its share price. Nafta closed at 1,373 crowns on Tuesday, far below the 2,000 crown level they held at the time of the sell-off.
The investment programme announced on Wednesday includes:
*A doubling of the present gas storage capacities from two to four billion cubic metres.
*Increasing natural gas production from its own Slovak resources.
*Launching crude oil production in Kazakhstan under a joint-venture with the Kazakh company, Anacon.
*The reconstruction of existing storage capacities.
"But they should have presented concrete details and plans for covering the investment," the international broker said.
"The remaining shareholders indeed did not seem to be convinced of plans presented in this form," he added.
-- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-563-3687
